images.title: Many answers or one?
images.purpose: Contrast a statistical question, whose answers vary, with one that has a single answer.
images.composition: Two panels side by side with a thin grey divider: on the left a group of dogs with different ages, on the right one child with one answer; plenty of white space in each panel.
exact_structure: Left panel heading Statistical in green (#009E73) with a small green tick.
Left panel: exactly 5 flat, simple dogs of different sizes in teal (#0072B2), each wearing a small round tag with its age in years: 2, 5, 1, 7, 3, from left to right.
Right panel heading Not statistical in vermilion (#D55E00) with a small vermilion cross.
Right panel: exactly 1 flat, faceless child figure in amber (#E69F00) holding a book, with one rounded tag beside it reading Yes.
A thin vertical grey (#6B7280) divider between the two panels.
rejection: more or fewer than 5 dogs, or any two dogs with the same age tag
more than one child or more than one answer tag on the right
questions written out in full sentences
images.takeaway: A question is statistical when answering it means collecting many values that vary.
images.description: Left: five dogs with age tags 2, 5, 1, 7 and 3 under the heading Statistical; right: one child with a book and the answer Yes under Not statistical.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how many answers each side needs, then name the question each side stands for.

image_decisions.why: Two contrasting panels show the many varying answers that mark a statistical question.
